title: Historical Aerial Photos of Berlin - Quick Summary
kicker: WALK OF BERLIN • LIVING IN BERLIN
items: **In 1928 Berlin photographed almost the whole city from a survey plane,** at a scale of 1:4,000. That is sharp enough to count the wings around your courtyard.
**The photos are free.** Geoportal Berlin publishes the old flights under the Datenlizenz Deutschland Zero, so you can look, download and reuse them.
**Open the year that fits your question:** 1928 for what stood before the war, 1953 for what the war left, and the newest colour photo for today.
**The 1979 flight is the second layer:** 717 photos of West Berlin from May 1979, so you can put the divided city next to 1928 and today.
**The quickest way in** is luftbilder.berlin.codefor.de: type your address and split the screen to compare two years.
**Read the street pattern first,** then the courtyards. A missing side wing is often a war gap, and a flat roof between pitched ones is usually its replacement.
**A sharp straight line where the grey tone jumps** is usually the edge of a photo sheet, not a demolished row.
**If you want to keep your street,** my print puts the 1928 photo above today's photo of the same ground, made to order.
**Aerial photos show roofs, not people.** For who lived in your house, use the Berlin address books.
